name: IBM
story: A research laboratory, enterprise distribution and compatible systems turned hardware into long-lived business infrastructure.

name: Apple
story: Integrated hardware, software and distribution connected personal computing to a larger device and services ecosystem.

name: Microsoft
story: Software licensing and developer tools established distribution that later extended into enterprise subscriptions and cloud infrastructure.

name: Intel
story: Process engineering and an instruction-set ecosystem helped scale microprocessors; later competition illustrates that technical leadership can change.

name: NVIDIA
story: Graphics processors and a programmable developer platform connected parallel computing to scientific work and machine learning.

name: AMD
story: Competing processor designs, graphics acquisitions and a fabless model created repeated opportunities to challenge incumbents.

name: Sony
story: Miniaturization, entertainment content and electronics engineering connected portable media to games, imaging and sensors.

name: Philips
story: Industrial research and consumer electronics standards preceded a later concentration in health technology.

name: Panasonic
story: Mass manufacturing and electronics engineering connected home appliances, audiovisual devices and batteries.

name: Toshiba
story: A diversified electronics company helped commercialize memory and portable computing. Its delisting prevents a continuous current public-security comparison.

name: Samsung Electronics
story: Manufacturing scale across memory, displays and devices supported a broad electronics ecosystem. No USD share-class history is mapped here.

name: Nintendo
story: Hardware design and owned game franchises developed a recurring interaction between devices, software and distribution.

name: Canon
story: Precision optics and manufacturing capabilities connected cameras, copying and printing.

name: HP / Hewlett-Packard lineage
story: Electronic instruments expanded into computers and printing; the 2015 separation means today’s HP equity is not the entire historical enterprise.

name: Nokia
story: Mobile-device scale gave way to a network-infrastructure business; product success and shareholder returns need not move together.

name: GE / GE Aerospace lineage
story: A diversified industrial research organization evolved through major separations. Current equity history does not represent ownership of every former business.

name: Siemens
story: Electrical engineering and industrial automation capabilities connected infrastructure, manufacturing and digital systems.

name: Boeing
story: Aircraft design, manufacturing and airline relationships scaled commercial aviation with substantial capital and execution risks.

name: Toyota
story: Production engineering and powertrain investment connected manufacturing discipline to hybrid vehicles.

name: Honda
story: Engine engineering and manufacturing connected motorcycles, cars and other mobility applications.

name: 3M
story: Materials research and manufacturing turned reusable technical capabilities into products across multiple industries.

name: Amazon
story: Retail logistics and reusable computing infrastructure supported marketplaces, cloud services and connected devices.

name: Alphabet / Google
story: Search relevance and advertising distribution supported investment in browsers, mobile systems and machine learning.

name: Tesla
story: Battery integration, software and manufacturing investment connected electric vehicles to energy storage.

name: Adobe
story: Publishing standards and creative software developed into recurring software subscriptions.

name: SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust
story: An investable US large-cap comparison beginning at its actual 1993 inception; no synthetic pre-inception fund returns.

name: Eastman Kodak — former common shares
story: Imaging research and a film-based distribution system produced important technology. The old common shares were cancelled in September 2013; today’s KODK is a different equity claim.
